name: Arto
description: 🅰️ Arto — the Art of Reading Markdown.

paragraphs: A desktop app that renders Markdown the way GitHub does, locally and offline.

Arto is beta. Features may change without regard to backward compatibility. macOS is the platform it is developed and tested on; Linux and Windows builds exist but are experimental — see Platform support.
Most Markdown tools are built for writing. Arto is built for reading: the name is short for "Art of Reading".
features: Reading — GitHub's dialect drawn with GitHub's own stylesheet: headings, tables, task lists, footnotes, autolinks and heading slugs; the five alerts (NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION); code highlighted per…

What the renderer reads — Markdown is a family of dialects, so the extensions are switches rather than assumptions: math, wiki links, superscript and subscript, definition lists, heading attributes and permalinks, smart…

Getting around — one panel with three faces rather than three panels: a file explorer holding as many folders as you need, the documents you have read grouped by day, and the ones you have starred (⌘1, ⌘2, ⌘3, and ⌘B to…

The gutter — a ruler stands in the page's own margin and marks every heading: its width is the heading's depth, its colour a pinned search, its thickness where you are. ⌘J opens it into a list of headings you can walk…

Finding — ⌘K fuzzy-matches one query the way fzf does, across the files under the folder you are in, what you have read, what you have kept, and every command by name — a command showing the keystroke that runs it,…
